angle: Coaches use the same tools; medium pace; winning weeks instead of streaks
hook: I coach women through fat loss. Right now, at 41, I'm in a fat-loss phase myself.
draft:
I'm 41, and I'm in a fat-loss phase right now.

It's a three-month plan at a medium pace. The target is 5 to 6 kg. Four workouts a week, 12,000 steps a day.

I'm sharing it because a lot of women assume coaches have it figured out. That we eat clean and our bodies just behave.

I competed in natural bodybuilding in December 2023. Before my Phuket trip this year I ran a 10-week cut. I still did it with a printed plan and a habit tracker, the same tools I give my clients.

Two things I hold myself to.

I pick a medium pace on purpose. A crash cut would fight with everything else in my week: clients, my sons, training. A plan I can keep for three months beats a plan I can survive for three weeks.

And I track weeks, not streaks. A streak breaks the first time a work trip or a bad night gets in the way, and that's usually when people quit. A week can still be a winning week with one bad day inside it.

None of this is glamorous. It's mostly walking, lifting, and writing things down.

What would a winning week look like for you, if it didn't have to be perfect?
final:
I coach women through fat loss. Right now, at 41, I'm in a fat-loss phase myself.

It's a three-month plan at a medium pace: a few kilos, four workouts a week and a lot of walking.

A lot of women assume coaches have this figured out, that we eat clean and our bodies behave. I competed in natural bodybuilding in December 2023, and before my Phuket trip this year I ran a 10-week cut. I did it with a printed plan and a habit tracker, the same tools I give my clients.

I chose a medium pace on purpose. A crash cut would fight with everything else in my week: clients, my sons, my own training. I'd rather keep a plan going for three months than survive three weeks of a harsh one.

I also track weeks instead of streaks. A streak breaks the first time a work trip or a bad night gets in the way, and that's usually when people give up. A week with one bad day in it can still be a winning week.

Most days it's a walk, a workout and a few lines in the tracker.

What would a winning week look like for you, if it didn't have to be perfect?
